### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

The security fixes and the versioning note are in
[v0.2.0-beta.1](https://github.com/OmarHung/DisplayMuxAuto/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta.1). This build
adds two reported fixes, **both of which affect the current stable release, 0.1.11**.

### Fixed: a display's input resetting itself to "not selected"

The scan emptied a display's stored input and input list **before** going to read them, and that
read is allowed to fail — a display answers the host it is showing and no other, so failing is
the ordinary case for the host that is off screen. On failure the values were already gone, and
the caller logged it and saved the settings anyway.

The value came back on whichever later scan managed to read, which is why it looked like an input
disappearing and then returning for no reason. The input list went with it, which made the next
scan treat the display as never read and try again.

Worst of it: **an input set by hand was discarded the same way** — and setting it by hand exists
precisely because this read cannot reach a computer the display has never shown.

Nothing stored is discarded now. A reading replaces it; the absence of one does not.

### Fixed: display merges never actually applied between two hosts

**Windows reads this MSI's serial number and macOS reads none from it.** Merges were matched on a
full fingerprint comparison, which counts "one side has a serial, the other does not" as a
difference.

So a merge made on Windows arrived on the Mac, was stored, and matched nothing there. The Mac
went on offering the same display for merging, and merging it again stored a second entry — and
since a merge card is labelled by manufacturer and product code only, the two were identical on
screen: one display merged into one display, listed twice.

Merges now use the rule the input notes have always used (whose comment says it outright: hosts
can read the same display's serial number differently).

**The change reaches only as far as a missing serial:**

- Two serials that are both present and different still mean two displays
- A serial present on one side only is treated as the same display
- **Switching is untouched** — a write still demands an exact fingerprint match against a display
  present right now, and refuses when more than one matches

Duplicate merges already stored are **collapsed to the newest when settings load**, so the
duplicate on screen goes away without unmerging anything.

### What to test

- **Merging across hosts**: merge on one computer, and confirm the other no longer offers the same
  display for merging.
- **Duplicates collapsing**: if you already merged twice, confirm only one card remains.
- **Different displays are not conflated**: confirm the MPG and the VG are still separate shared
  displays with independent inputs.
- **Inputs staying put**: switch one display to the other host, so this one cannot read it, and
  confirm its stored input survives.
- Set an input by hand, make that display unreadable, and confirm the value is still there.

### Known limitations

- The **contents** of a reply are still unauthenticated (see the beta.1 notes).
- The pairing password is used directly as the HMAC key with no KDF, and the minimum is still
  eight characters.
- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.
